title: Fire and Gas Detection System

introduction.definition: A fire and gas (F&G) detection system watches a process area for gas leaks and fires. Point and open-path gas detectors, flame detectors, heat and smoke detectors and manual call points feed a SIL-rated logic panel that raises alarms and starts executive actions such as shutdown, isolation, deluge and ventilation changes.
applications: Process modules, compressor and pump areas
Offshore platforms, terminals and tank farms
key_points: Alarm at 20 % LEL, action at ≈ 50–60 % LEL
introduction.summary: A fire and gas detection system uses gas, flame, heat and smoke detectors and manual call points around a process area to detect leaks and fires early, raise alarms and trigger shutdown, deluge and ventilation actions.

pressure.title: Coverage: see the fire, smell the gas — then act
pressure.description: F&G detectors are placed by coverage mapping: flame detectors have a cone of vision (≈ 90° for UV/IR) and a range for a given fire size; gas detectors are placed where leaks would collect (low for heavier-than-air gas, high for lighter) and open-path detectors guard boundaries. Typical alarm levels: 20 % LEL low, 50–60 % LEL high. The F&G logic uses voting (e.g. 2-out-of-N confirmed) to start executive actions: shutdown and isolation, deluge, ventilation changes and alarms.

script.narration: This module introduces the Fire and Gas Detection System.
A fire and gas (F&G) detection system watches a process area for gas leaks and fires.

Point and open-path gas detectors, flame detectors, heat and smoke detectors and manual call points feed a SIL-rated logic panel that raises alarms and starts executive actions such as shutdown, isolation, deluge and ventilation changes.
Typical applications include process modules, compressor and pump areas; offshore platforms, terminals and tank farms.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Fire and Gas Detection System works.
Gas leaks from a flange.
Point and open-path detectors sense it.
Flame detectors watch their cones of vision.
The F&G panel votes and acts.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

F&G detectors are placed by coverage mapping: flame detectors have a cone of vision (≈ 90° for UV/IR) and a range for a given fire size; gas detectors are placed where leaks would collect (low for heavier-than-air gas, high for lighter) and open-path detectors guard boundaries.

video_tutorials.title: Fire and Gas Detection System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Fire and Gas Detection System.
Check panel faults / inhibits.
Bump-test gas detectors; clean optics.
Full cause & effect proof test.
Watch for detector blinded: fault / no response. Common cause: dirty optics, blocked view.
Watch for spurious trip: unplanned shutdown. Common cause: single-detector logic, interference.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
